metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most follow-up questions are about specific output: one quotes the reported 'Missing lung side (528 records)' finding and asks how it can occur under a valid schema, and others ask about the added generics, a missing heading, and why chestradqwen has only one flag.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: Every applicable rule file was in context (the general, coding, git and Python rules and mesa-build's CLAUDE.md; the litellm AGENTS.md files are vendored .venv files), and the code broadly complies, with typed locals and Google-style docstrings in batch_corrector.py and correction_rules.py, but compliance is partial: three of the six commit subjects break the 50-character limit ('feat(datagen): add add_items, dedupe and flag actions' is 53, and 'feat(pipelines): add chestradqwen correction config' and 'feat: support flag rules in correction config skill' are 51 each).

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 14 of 809 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: The median is 26 generated lines per producing prompt across 11 prompts, which places the branch in band 3, and the prompts name units of work (a run-status mechanism, no ids in files, a default path when there are no rules); the one outlier is a single prompt that bundled add_items, dedupe, the flag route and the rules into 769 lines.
